original_review.note: Reproduced with limit_grandchild.py: Claude reports a grandchild of a parent dropped at CHILD_LIMIT with parent_sid None, so _stamp_child's final else (daemon.py:135-136) stamps it from the relayed turn. 94dd73c4 fixes the first-subagent_event and non-start cases but NOT this parent_sid=None case (c6-fu-r1 rb1).

Reproduced: deleting the `elif parent and parent in seen: stamp = None` branch (daemon.py:133-134) leaves relay_provenance_check (16 tests) and permissions_check relay_provenance_checks (26396 checks) passing. Pinned in 94dd73c4.

Traced: _idle_event passes idle=True (daemon.py:1597) so a child announced after the turn's result is marked seen with no stamp and never gets one. Native ordering is unverified; 94dd73c4 adds a Claude pre-stamp from the Agent call (Codex not).
CHILD_SEEN=4096 and `seen.pop(next(iter(seen)))` (daemon.py:67,128-129): an evicted live child is new again and stamped from the running turn. Fixed in 94dd73c4 (grow-only seen set).

entries.mechanism: A Codex sub-agent's approval never reaches the child's stamp. codex.py calls the permit with widening=... and subagent_sid=<cx:sid> but no `subagent` label (providers/codex.py:2318-2331), so build_permit's who=subagent_origin(...) is None and the call is treated as the orchestrator's: the reader is asked with child=None and the card follows the turn running when it asks. A Codex background child of a relayed turn that asks after the turn ended shows no line, and a Codex child of an owner turn that asks while a later relayed turn runs is labelled 'turn started by a message from chat S' (kind 'started' at r3+), the exact case the round-1 MED fix was meant to close. The description/docs claim Codex children are covered ('Codex passes it on every child approval'); the tests only pass because they call the permit with subagent='bg' (or 'c' in the matrix), a call shape the real Codex provider never makes. At this head build_permit sets child = sid if who is not None else None (permissions.py:989), so relay_child is None for every Codex child widening.

entries.mechanism: A child stamped by chat S1's relayed turn keeps kind 'started' naming S1 when a later relayed turn from chat S2 re-tasks it; stamps are never revisited, so its cards never say S2 is running/carrying words to it, while the orchestrator's card in the same turn names S2. The 'running' fix of round 2 covers only unstamped children.

non_issues.claim: A card raised in a relayed turn should not offer Always.
A bridge (jarvis-mcp dangerous tool) call from a relay-spawned background child shows no line after the relayed turn ends.
non_issues.why_not: Deliberate: the bridge cannot tell a child from the orchestrator, so its asks are unattributed, 'running' at most (control-plane.md:396-400; hud-api.md:3683-3686).

non_issues.claim: A relay-spawned child whose first hook beats the daemon's record of its start shows 'while ... runs' instead of 'started'.
non_issues.why_not: Documented: a child the daemon never saw is treated as unattributed ('running' while a relay runs; control-plane.md:392-395). It still names the chat, and it is not a wrong attribution.

non_issues.claim: A relayed_from without kind (or with an unknown kind) is drawn as 'while ... runs'; it should default to 'started'.
non_issues.why_not: Intended fail-safe: hud-api.md:3680-3688 says the HUD draws the 'running' wording for any kind but 'started'; the daemon always sends kind.

non_issues.claim: The 8-hex thread-id check (_RELAY_THREAD_ID, the HUD regex) drops real thread ids.
non_issues.why_not: Thread ids are secrets.token_hex(4), 8 lowercase hex (jarvis/v2/stores.py:173); the tests' expected() uses the real chat.id.
